candidates.original_title: Computer-based brief intervention a randomized trial with postpartum women
candidates.description: A single 20-minute computer-delivered brief intervention reduced self-reported drug use among postpartum women at 4-month follow-up
candidates.citation_sentence: The present study was designed to replicate the results of Ondersma et al. (2007) with respect to postpartum drug use.
candidates.notes: Results differ across timepoints: 7-day point-prevalence abstinence significant at 3 months (p = .01) but not at 6 months (p = .456); days of drug use non-significant at both timepoints; authors report mixed support, stating both 'support the short-term efficacy' and that findings 'provide support for the previous trial' while noting decline by 6 months.

candidates.original_title: Computer-based brief intervention: A randomized trial with postpartum women
candidates.description: The original study claimed that a single 20-minute computer-delivered e-SBI intervention plus two non-tailored mailings reduced postpartum women's illicit drug use compared with a control condition.
candidates.citation_sentence: For example, in a randomized trial with 107 postpartum women, Ondersma, Svikis, and Schuster (2007) showed that a single 20-minute e-SBI intervention plus two non-tailored mailings was associated with reductions in self-reported drug use at a 4-month follow-up.
candidates.notes: The replication found significant short-term support for biologically confirmed abstinence at 3 months, but no significant effect at 6 months and no significant effects on days of drug use; the authors describe the findings as supporting short-term efficacy.

prior_source_review.finding: Original intervention included mailings; the replication removed them. Three-month abstinence improved, six-month point-prevalence and use-frequency measures did not. Descriptions lack a common endpoint/timepoint, so success/inconclusive agreement is not interpretable until scope is fixed.
prior_source_review.evidence: following participants to 6 months, using TLFB to measure drug-using days, and using only the e-SBI without any incentives or motivational mailings.
